{"id": "ede5716a-e513-49f4-bfd4-0b5b31ad5b7c", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "A Windows Server 2016 patch run is failing. Here is the collected evidence; diagnose the root cause from it.

CBS.log excerpt:
  Loaded Servicing Stack v10.0.14393.5210
  Failed to load the manifest for component. The servicing stack version does not support this package format. [HRESULT = 0x800f0831 - CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION]
  Servicing stack must be updated before this package can be installed. Required SSU: KB5062561 (10.0.14393.6xxx), present SSU: 10.0.14393.5210.
  WU client called DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
  RestoreHealth: no corrupt payload detected in component store; store scan returned clean. Operation completed. [HRESULT = 0x0 - S_OK]
  Appl: Re-evaluating package Package_for_KB5062560, 0x800f0831 recurs.
  No pending.xml present; SessionsPending empty; DataStore.edb size 42 MB (nominal).

Servicing state: OS build 10.0.14393.6252; installed SSU 10.0.14393.5210; required SSU KB5062561 pending and NOT installed; no pending transactions; DataStore.edb nominal; no Windows.old.

Explain specifically why DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth completes with exit code 0 yet the cumulative update keeps failing with the same 0x800F0831 error, and what the correct fix is.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "b0f090bc-8ee0-4662-96ef-cf0cbc5e4e99", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_10mkrrvT1vW4mFN6GRrleG", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: ec2-patch-windows-servicing-store\\\\ndescription: >-\\\\n  Recover a Windows Server (2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025) EC2 instance whose\\\\n  patching is blocked by a component-servicing fault \\\\u2014 the family of failures\\\\n  rooted in CBS/WinSxS, the servicing stack (SSU), pending servicing\\\\n  transactions, the Windows Update datastore, or a stalled feature update. Use\\\\n  when a patch or Windows Update install fails with 0x80073712, 0x800F0831\\\\n  (CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION), 0x800F081F, 0x800F0922, 0x80073701, 0x80070BC9,\\\\n  0x8024400A/0x80244010, or 0xC1900101; when DISM/ScanHealth reports corruption\\\\n  or \\\\\"packages are pending servicing\\\\\"; when updates stick in\\\\n  \\\\\"InstalledPendingReboot\\\\\"/\\\\\"Pending Install\\\\\"; when DataStore.edb is oversized; or\\\\n  when Windows.old lingers after a failed in-place upgrade. This skill diagnoses\\\\n  WHICH servicing fault is present and applies the correct, ordered recovery \\\\u2014\\\\n  the sub-faults interact (a stale SSU and pending transactions both surface AS\\\\n  store corruption), so the naive \\\\\"just run DISM /RestoreHealth\\\\\" loops without\\\\n  converging.\\\\nlicense: Apache-2.0\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  author: \\\\\"sulbri\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"Chat tasks, Incident RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EC2, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Windows Server, Patching\\\\\"\\\\n  domains: \\\\\"EC2, SSM, Patch Manager, Windows Update, CBS, DISM, WinSxS, SSU\\\\\"\\\\n  platforms: \\\\\"Windows\\\\\"\\\\n  supported-os: \\\\\"Windows Server 2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025\\\\\"\\\\n  operation-type: \\\\\"read-and-mutate\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Recover a Windows component-servicing fault blocking patching\\\\n\\\\n## When this applies\\\\nA Windows patch / Windows Update install fails and the signature points at the\\\\ncomponent-servicing subsystem (CBS/WinSxS, servicing stack, pending\\\\ntransactions, WU datastore, or feature-update state). Instance is Online in SSM.\\\\nIf the failure is a *connectivity* fault (WSUS/TLS/proxy) or a *policy* blocker\\\\n(GPO/AV/BitLocker), this is the wrong skill \\\\u2014 those are separate domains.\\\\n\\\\n## The key insight: diagnose the sub-fault first \\\\u2014 they masquerade as each other\\\\n`0x800F0831` / \\\\\"store corruption\\\\\" is the most common *surface* symptom, but its\\\\n*cause* is often not store corruption at all:\\\\n- an **outdated servicing stack (SSU)** can\\'t process a new LCU manifest \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **halted pending transaction** (interrupted reboot) \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **stalled feature update** leaves mixed package state \\\\u2192 LCU \\\\\"not applicable\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\nRunning `DISM /RestoreHealth` blindly loops for hours when the real cause is a\\\\nstale SSU or a pending transaction. **Identify the sub-fault, then apply the\\\\nmatching path in the correct order.**\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnosis first (always)\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Capture the failing error code and the servicing state before changing anything:\\\\n  ```powershell\\\\n  DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth\\\\n  DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String \\\\\"Pending\\\\\"\\\\n  Test-Path \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\servicing\\\\\\\\Packages\\\\\\\\pending.xml\\\\\"\\\\n  (Get-Item \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\SoftwareDistribution\\\\\\\\DataStore\\\\\\\\DataStore.edb\\\\\").Length/1MB\\\\n  Get-ChildItem \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Windows.old\\\\\",\\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\`$WINDOWS.~BT\\\\\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\\\\n  Get-Content \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Logs\\\\\\\\CBS\\\\\\\\CBS.log\\\\\" -Tail 80 | Select-String \\\\\"ERROR|corrupt|pending|missing\\\\\"\\\\n  ```\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Route to the sub-fault by signature (load the matching reference for exact steps):\\\\n  - Pending transactions present (`pending.xml`, \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\", `0x800F0922`) \\\\u2192 read [pending transactions](reference/pending-transactions.md) \\\\u2014 clear these BEFORE any DISM repair.\\\\n  - SSU outdated / `0x80070BC9` / `0x80073701` on LCU \\\\u2192 read [SSU ordering](reference/ssu-ordering.md) \\\\u2014 install SSU BEFORE the LCU and before RestoreHealth.\\\\n  - Genuine CBS/WinSxS corruption (`0x80073712`, `0x800F0831` with no pending/SSU cause) \\\\u2192 read [CBS store repair](reference/cbs-store-repair.md).\\\\n  - WU datastore bloat/corruption (`0x8024400A`, `DataStore.edb` >1GB, ESENT 455/489) \\\\u2192 read [WU datastore](reference/wu-datastore.md).\\\\n  - Stalled feature update (`0xC1900101`, lingering `Windows.old`) \\\\u2192 read [feature update state](reference/feature-update.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Ordered recovery (dependencies matter \\\\u2014 do not reorder)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Clear pending transactions first.** `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions`;\\\\n  rename a stale (`>24h`) `pending.xml`; clear `SessionsPending`. A pending transaction poisons every later step.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **Bring the servicing stack current.** Install any pending Servicing Stack Update BEFORE the LCU.\\\\n  An old SSU cannot process a new LCU manifest and will re-manifest as store corruption.\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Repair the component store** only after 3\\\\u20134: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`\\\\n  (add `/Source:WIM:<path>\\\\\\\\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess` on isolated fleets where WU is blocked), then `sfc /scannow`.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Reset WU components** if the datastore is implicated: stop `wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver`;\\\\n  rename `SoftwareDistribution` and `catroot2`; restart. See the datastore reference for the `DataStore.edb` specifics.\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: **Reboot** to let TrustedInstaller finalize valid pending operations, then re-scan.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\nDo not report the instance patchable until you confirm each of these:\\\\n- [ ] `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth` reports the store **healthy** (not just \\\\\"RestoreHealth exit 0\\\\\").\\\\n- [ ] No packages remain \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\"/\\\\\"Uninstall Pending\\\\\" and `pending.xml` is absent.\\\\n- [ ] No Servicing Stack Update is still pending (`Search(\\\\\"IsInstalled=0\\\\\")` returns no \\\\\"Servicing Stack\\\\\" title).\\\\n- [ ] The original failing update/patch scan re-run no longer returns its original error code.\\\\n- [ ] `wuauserv` is Running.\\\\nIf any check fails, consult the matching reference\\'s escalation section rather than re-looping DISM.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **SSU installs are forward-only \\\\u2014 they cannot be uninstalled.** Do not promise a rollback of the servicing stack.\\\\n- **Order is load-bearing:** pending-transaction clear \\\\u2192 SSU \\\\u2192 RestoreHealth \\\\u2192 SFC \\\\u2192 reboot. SFC before a healthy store just fails; RestoreHealth before clearing a pending transaction loops.\\\\n- **A recent `pending.xml` (<24h) may be valid** \\\\u2014 renaming it can abort a legitimate in-flight servicing operation. Check age first.\\\\n- **`/Source` build must match the running OS build exactly** (`Version` + UBR); a mismatched WIM fails RestoreHealth with a generic error.\\\\n- **On an isolated/patched fleet, WU as the RestoreHealth source is blocked** \\\\u2014 supply an explicit `/Source` with `/LimitAccess` or the repair silently retries WU and times out.\\\\n- **A stalled feature update is NOT store corruption** \\\\u2014 running RestoreHealth against a half-upgraded image (\\\\\"not applicable to this image\\\\\") wastes the maintenance window; resolve the upgrade state first.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"automation/iam-policy.json\", \"reference/pending-transactions.md\", \"reference/wu-datastore.md\", \"reference/feature-update.md\", \"reference/ssu-ordering.md\", \"reference/cbs-store-repair.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "3fa41cd1-5bc6-411b-9944-a39c486ce693", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_zZxZWWrePgLQzOWJA7XG6n", "content": "[{'text': '# Servicing Stack Update (SSU) ordering (install BEFORE the LCU)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80070BC9` (ERROR_FAIL_NOACTION_REBOOT), `0x80073701`\\n(ERROR_SXS_ASSEMBLY_MISSING) on LCU; CBS.log \"Servicing stack must be updated before this\\npackage can be installed\"; LCU downloads then fails at \"Installing\"; Server 2016 stuck on old CU.\\n\\n**Why:** the servicing stack is what *processes* update manifests. An outdated SSU cannot parse a\\nnewer LCU manifest, and the failure surfaces as store corruption \u2014 so RestoreHealth \"fixes\"\\nnothing. SSU must be current first.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Report OS build + servicing stack:\\n   ```powershell\\n   $os=Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem\\n   \"$($os.Caption) Build $($os.BuildNumber).$((Get-ItemProperty \\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows NT\\\\CurrentVersion\\').UBR)\"\\n   ```\\n2. Find pending SSU vs LCU (SSU installs separately on 2016; combined on 2019+):\\n   ```powershell\\n   $s=(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search(\"IsInstalled=0 and Type=\\'Software\\'\").Updates\\n   $s|?{$_.Title -match \\'Servicing Stack\\'}|%{ \"SSU: $($_.Title)\" }\\n   ```\\n3. Install the SSU first (download+install just the \"Servicing Stack\" updates via\\n   `Microsoft.Update.Session`; ResultCode 2=Succeeded, 3=SucceededWithErrors), then let the LCU proceed.\\n4. Re-evaluate the component store: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup`.\\n5. Verify no SSU remains pending before installing the LCU.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- Server 2012 R2: download SSU from Microsoft Update Catalog, install via `wusa.exe`; SHA-2 chain may be required.\\n- Server 2016: specific LCUs require a specific SSU version \u2014 check the KB prerequisites.\\n- WSUS: ensure the SSU (not just the LCU) is approved.\\n- 2019+: ensure the combined SSU+LCU package is being offered.\\n- Since 2024, a SafeOS/WinRE update may also be required.\\n- **SSU is forward-only \u2014 it cannot be uninstalled.**\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "a306653d-c4b2-446d-9a5d-191362166a11", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## Root cause

This is **not** component-store corruption — it's an **outdated servicing stack** that can't process the new cumulative update's manifest, and that failure is simply surfacing *as* `CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION`.

**Why `RestoreHealth` exits 0 but the patch still fails:**

- `DISM /RestoreHealth` validates and repairs the **WinSxS component store itself** — checking payload files against manifests already known to the servicing stack, and replacing corrupt files from a source. The scan comes back clean (`S_OK`) because the store genuinely *isn't* corrupt — there's nothing for RestoreHealth to find or fix.
- The actual blocker is upstream of that: the installed servicing stack (**10.0.14393.5210**) is being asked to parse the manifest format shipped in `Package_for_KB5062560` (targeting build **10.0.14393.6252**), and it's too old to understand it. The CBS.log line makes this explicit: *"Servicing stack must be updated before this package can be installed. Required SSU: KB5062561 (10.0.14393.6xxx), present SSU: 10.0.14393.5210."*
- Since the servicing stack — not the store — is what's deficient, re-running RestoreHealth re-evaluates the same package against the same outdated stack and reproduces `0x800F0831` every time. It's a loop that can never converge, because the tool is repairing a healthy subsystem while the real gate (SSU version) goes untouched.
- The rest of the evidence rules out the other sub-faults that commonly masquerade as this error: no `pending.xml`, empty `SessionsPending` (no halted transaction), nominal `DataStore.edb` (no WU datastore bloat), no `Windows.old` (no stalled feature upgrade). SSU-vs-LCU mismatch is the only fault signature left standing.

## Correct fix

Install the required SSU **before** retrying the LCU — do not run further `RestoreHealth` passes first:

1. Confirm current build/SSU state (already have this): build `10.0.14393.6252`, installed SSU `10.0.14393.5210`, required SSU `KB5062561`.
2. Download and install **KB5062561** (the standalone SSU — on Server 2016 the SSU ships separately from the LCU, unlike 2019+ combined packages) directly, e.g. via `wusa.exe` or the Microsoft Update Catalog package — don't rely on WU/WSUS surfacing it only alongside the LCU if it's stuck.
3. Reboot if required by the SSU install (SSU installs are forward-only — it cannot be uninstalled later).
4. Re-run `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup` to let the now-current servicing stack re-evaluate component state.
5. Verify no SSU remains pending (`IsInstalled=0` search for "Servicing Stack" titles returns empty), then retry the cumulative update (`KB5062560`).
6. If using WSUS, confirm the SSU — not just the LCU — is approved for this group; a common cause of this exact loop is the SSU never being approved/offered even though the LCU is.

If after installing KB5062561 the LCU still fails with the same code, that would point to genuine CBS corruption and warrant the store-repair path — but given the evidence here, the SSU gap is almost certainly the whole story.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
